summary: The selected scroll is blessed. C enters read.c:seffect_genocide, then do_class_genocide; its class prompt accepts the answer newt through the monster-name fallback. The original JavaScript gap at seffects caused the step-24 mismatch. B34 ports the complete class and species genocide family with independent uncursed, cursed, confused, and throne recordings; the selected case now matches all 31 steps.

source.branch: read.c:seffect_genocide determines known scroll status, prints discovery feedback, then chooses do_class_genocide for blessed scrolls or do_genocide((!cursed) | (2 * Confusion)) otherwise. The selected blessed case reaches do_class_genocide, and its answer newt is converted to a monster class through name_to_mon fallback. Independent B34 recordings exercise do_genocide through uncursed, cursed, confused, and throne callers.
callers: read.c:seffects SCR_GENOCIDE arm calls seffect_genocide after doread; B34 wires js/read.js:seffects to the ported wrapper.
sit.c throne arm calls do_genocide(5); B34 wires js/sit.js:dosit to that active caller and verifies it with an independent recording.
dependencies: mondata.c:name_to_mon is already ported in js/mondata.js and is needed for selected species names. insight.c:num_genocides and list_genocided are available in js/insight.js for conduct and question-mark responses.
mon.c:kill_genocided_monsters is currently a partial gap in js/do.js; C discards its result but its state effect must remain named as an unported gap until the full mon.c function is ported.
Check read.c:getlin prompt, monster-vitals flags, object inventory update, polymorph, death, and cursed monster creation in source order. Do not infer those paths from the selected newt case.

evidence: Current saved challenges/evaluations/20260927175933-v9.json leaves 7 of 31 screens unmatched, first at segment 0 step 24. A fresh scan at b6e28d15 reports note_unported(read.c seffect_genocide) and the same first screen mismatch; RNG totals alone do not prove the prompt and state path match.

The independently recorded C recipe challenges/cases/v9/genocide-scroll-selects-species.recipe.session.json reaches a blessed genocide scroll and answers newt at the class prompt. B34 source tracing corrected the earlier ordinary-species attribution; this case alone does not exercise do_genocide.

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/read.c:seffect_genocide at lines 1722-1738 calls do_class_genocide or do_genocide; do_class_genocide at 2638 and do_genocide at 2826 implement the prompts and effects. read.c:seffects calls the wrapper at 2240; sit.c also invokes do_genocide(5) from a throne.

At combined commit 85e2d70dee8d90a18baf62ee852ba83e8102b18d, challenges/evaluations/20260927230232-v9.json measures the selected case at 31/31 screens and cursors, 3298/3298 RNG, with no replay error. Five independent B34 recordings cover blessed class, uncursed species, cursed summon, confused self-genocide, and throne genocide paths.
